messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: second y-axis
parts:
Tomek,

There have been many posts about this on this listserv and
stackoverflow. Basic answer: no*. Other options include faceting your
graph, normalizing your y's to a common scale, or I guess fake it by
manually rescaling and labeling one series. Basically, if this is
something you really need to do, probably look to another graphics
package.

Ben

* HW quote on the subject: "I'm against this technique because I
believe it leads to serious visual distortions and meaningless
graphics."

messages.author: 8109194fbbaf9486
messages.subject: Re: second y-axis
parts:
I agree with the general philosophy. That said there are legitimate uses of the multiple axis feature. First, as a tool for data exploration (and not to demonstrate statistical relationships ), multiple axes are invaluable as a first look at time series relationships. Second, as has been pointed out elsewhere there are cases like multiple units for the same time series (Celsius v Fahrenheit) which require multiple axes.

I have considered normalizing, multiple faces (nrow=2) but all these have problems.

I would beg the ggplot developers to consider adding the feature.

The other thing I really miss is the ability to specify time series x-axis labeling breaks to be based on end of period (eg month) dates instead of beginning of next period (next month) dates.



Cheers, Anil
